title: The Persistence of Marketing Effects on Sales
author_source: Dekimpe, M. G. & Hanssens, D. M., Marketing Science 14(1), 1-21, 1995, article
note: Foundational paper introducing unit-root testing and VAR/impulse-response persistence analysis to marketing; distinguishes temporary vs. permanent (long-run) advertising effects on sales. Clear decision flow (stationary vs. evolving series -> VAR in levels vs. differences vs. VECM) that maps directly onto a lecture on stationarity.
course_use: Core reading (session on unit roots and persistence); paid journal, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Sustained Spending and Persistent Response: A New Look at Long-Term Marketing Profitability
author_source: Dekimpe, M. G. & Hanssens, D. M., Journal of Marketing Research 36(4), 397-412, 1999, article
note: Defines four strategic scenarios (business as usual, escalation, hysteresis, evolving business practice) from combinations of stationary/evolving sales and marketing spending; VECM-based. Useful 2x2 framework for discussing long-term profitability of marketing.
course_use: Core reading / discussion; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Time-series models in marketing: Past, present and future
author_source: Dekimpe, M. G. & Hanssens, D. M., International Journal of Research in Marketing 17(2-3), 183-193, 2000, article
note: Short review (11 pp.) of univariate ARIMA, transfer functions, VAR, unit roots and cointegration applications in marketing; good map of the method landscape. Dated in its future outlook but an ideal entry reading.
course_use: Background / first reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Modeling Marketing Dynamics by Time Series Econometrics
author_source: Pauwels, K., Currim, I., Dekimpe, M. G., Hanssens, D. M., Mizik, N., Ghysels, E. & Naik, P., Marketing Letters 15(4), 167-183, 2004, article
note: Choice-symposium overview: when to use VAR/VECM, persistence modelling, state-space and mixed-frequency approaches for marketing questions; discusses data requirements and managerial interpretation of impulse responses. Compact methods primer.
course_use: Core/background reading for VAR session; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Market Response, Competitive Behavior, and Time Series Analysis
author_source: Hanssens, D. M., Journal of Marketing Research 17(4), 470-485, 1980, article
note: Early classic applying Box-Jenkins/transfer-function identification and causality testing to sales response and competitive reactions across marketing-mix instruments. Historical anchor showing how ARIMA identification is used to specify response models.
course_use: Background / classic; paid (JSTOR), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Intervention Analysis with Applications to Economic and Environmental Problems
author_source: Box, G. E. P. & Tiao, G. C., Journal of the American Statistical Association 70(349), 70-79, 1975, article
note: Original intervention (pulse/step) analysis within ARIMA models; the template for evaluating discrete events such as a campaign launch, price change, regulation or market entry in a sales series.
course_use: Methods reference for intervention-analysis lab; paid (JSTOR/T&F), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Investigating Causal Relations by Econometric Models and Cross-spectral Methods
author_source: Granger, C. W. J., Econometrica 37(3), 424-438, 1969, article
note: Original definition of Granger causality. Use alongside marketing applications to teach what temporal-precedence tests can and cannot claim (not true causality).
course_use: Methods background (Granger causality); paid (JSTOR), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Co-Integration and Error Correction: Representation, Estimation, and Testing
author_source: Engle, R. F. & Granger, C. W. J., Econometrica 55(2), 251-276, 1987, article
note: Defines cointegration and the two-step error-correction estimator; basis for long-run equilibrium models such as sales vs. advertising or brand vs. category sales. Technical; assign selected sections.
course_use: Methods reference (cointegration); paid (JSTOR), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Estimation and Hypothesis Testing of Cointegration Vectors in Gaussian Vector Autoregressive Models
author_source: Johansen, S., Econometrica 59(6), 1551-1580, 1991, article
note: Johansen trace/max-eigenvalue cointegration tests used in most marketing VECM applications (e.g., Dekimpe & Hanssens 1999). Highly technical; reference for the test as implemented in R (urca) and Stata.
course_use: Methods reference only; paid (JSTOR), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Distribution of the Estimators for Autoregressive Time Series With a Unit Root
author_source: Dickey, D. A. & Fuller, W. A., Journal of the American Statistical Association 74(366), 427-431, 1979, article
note: Source of the (augmented) Dickey-Fuller unit-root test, the first diagnostic step in persistence modelling. Short (5 pp.) but mathematical.
course_use: Methods reference; paid (JSTOR), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Testing the null hypothesis of stationarity against the alternative of a unit root
author_source: Kwiatkowski, D., Phillips, P. C. B., Schmidt, P. & Shin, Y., Journal of Econometrics 54(1-3), 159-178, 1992, article
note: KPSS test with stationarity as the null; teach as a confirmatory complement to ADF (marketing studies often report both). Useful for showing conflicting test outcomes in a lab.
course_use: Methods reference for unit-root lab; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Seasonal integration and cointegration
author_source: Hylleberg, S., Engle, R. F., Granger, C. W. J. & Yoo, B. S., Journal of Econometrics 44(1-2), 215-238, 1990, article
note: HEGY test for seasonal unit roots; relevant when deciding between seasonal dummies and seasonal differencing (SARIMA) in quarterly or monthly sales data. Technical.
course_use: Methods reference (seasonality); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Generalized impulse response analysis in linear multivariate models
author_source: Pesaran, H. H. & Shin, Y., Economics Letters 58(1), 17-29, 1998, article
note: Generalized impulse response functions that do not depend on Cholesky variable ordering; standard choice in marketing VAR papers (e.g., Trusov et al. 2009). Short; explains the ordering problem students hit in labs.
course_use: Methods reference for IRF session; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Computation and analysis of multiple structural change models
author_source: Bai, J. & Perron, P., Journal of Applied Econometrics 18(1), 1-22, 2003, article
note: Practical algorithm and tests for multiple unknown structural breaks (implemented in R strucchange). Useful for detecting regime shifts in sales series, e.g., after market entry, crises or COVID. Crossref lists online year 2002, print issue 2003.
course_use: Methods reference (structural breaks lab); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Long-Term Effects of Price Promotions on Category Incidence, Brand Choice, and Purchase Quantity
author_source: Pauwels, K., Hanssens, D. M. & Siddarth, S., Journal of Marketing Research 39(4), 421-439, 2002, article
note: VAR/impulse-response decomposition of promotion effects into incidence, choice and quantity; promotion effects are mostly temporary and dissipate within weeks. Strong exemplar for reading IRF plots and short- vs. long-run elasticities.
course_use: Core application reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Category-Demand Effects of Price Promotions
author_source: Nijs, V. R., Dekimpe, M. G., Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M. & Hanssens, D. M., Marketing Science 20(1), 1-22, 2001, article
note: Persistence modelling across 560 categories over four years (Dutch market data); permanent category effects are rare. Classic empirical generalisation via unit-root tests plus VAR, with a second-stage regression of IRF-based elasticities on category traits.
course_use: Core application / empirical generalisation; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Competitive Reactions to Advertising and Promotion Attacks
author_source: Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., Nijs, V. R., Hanssens, D. M. & Dekimpe, M. G., Marketing Science 24(1), 35-54, 2005, article
note: VAR-based analysis of competitive reactions in several hundred categories (Dutch data); passive reaction is the dominant response. Good for teaching cross-brand impulse responses and competitive dynamics.
course_use: Application reading / seminar presentation; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Do Promotions Benefit Manufacturers, Retailers, or Both?
author_source: Srinivasan, S., Pauwels, K., Hanssens, D. M. & Dekimpe, M. G., Management Science 50(5), 617-629, 2004, article
note: VAR models on revenue and margin series for manufacturers and the retailer (Dominick's Finer Foods scanner data). Shows how impulse responses translate into profitability outcomes; the Dominick's data are publicly available for replication.
course_use: Application / replication idea with Dominick's data; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Effects of Word-of-Mouth versus Traditional Marketing: Findings from an Internet Social Networking Site
author_source: Trusov, M., Bucklin, R. E. & Pauwels, K., Journal of Marketing 73(5), 90-102, 2009, article
note: Very teachable VAR: Granger causality tests, generalized IRFs and long-term elasticities of WOM referrals vs. media and events on sign-ups. Compact (13 pp.), clear elasticity tables; often used as a model paper for student projects.
course_use: Core reading + lab template (Granger, VAR, GIRF); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Creating lift versus building the base: Current trends in marketing dynamics
author_source: Leeflang, P. S. H., Bijmolt, T. H. A., van Doorn, J., Hanssens, D. M., van Heerde, H. J., Verhoef, P. C. & Wieringa, J. E., International Journal of Research in Marketing 26(1), 13-20, 2009, article
note: Short overview of dynamic marketing models (VAR, state-space, dynamic linear models, distributed lags), classifying short-term lift vs. long-term base effects. Good conceptual framing reading.
course_use: Background reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Econometric Measurement of the Duration of Advertising Effect on Sales
author_source: Clarke, D. G., Journal of Marketing Research 13(4), 345-357, 1976, article
note: Meta-analysis of advertising carryover (Koyck/distributed-lag) estimates showing that measured duration depends on the data interval (data-interval bias). Classic anchor for adstock and distributed-lag teaching.
course_use: Core reading (distributed lags/adstock); paid (JSTOR), WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Generalizing What Is Known About Temporal Aggregation and Advertising Carryover
author_source: Leone, R. P., Marketing Science 14(3_supplement), G141-G150, 1995, article
note: Empirical generalisation: after correcting for temporal aggregation, advertising effects last roughly 6-9 months. Short; pairs with Clarke (1976) for an adstock half-life discussion.
course_use: Background reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Optimal Data Interval for Estimating Advertising Response
author_source: Tellis, G. J. & Franses, P. H., Marketing Science 25(3), 217-229, 2006, article
note: Shows when temporally aggregated data bias carryover estimates and which data interval suffices (Koyck model). Directly relevant when students choose weekly vs. monthly vs. quarterly data across countries.
course_use: Methods reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: How Well Does Advertising Work? Generalizations from Meta-Analysis of Brand Advertising Elasticities
author_source: Sethuraman, R., Tellis, G. J., Briesch, R. A., Journal of Marketing Research 48(3), 457-471, 2011, article
note: Meta-analysis of several hundred brand advertising elasticities: average short-term elasticity about 0.1, long-term about 0.2; moderators include region (Europe vs US), product life cycle stage, data interval and model specification. Benchmark for judging students' own estimates.
course_use: Core benchmark reading for the advertising elasticity session. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Empirical Generalizations About Market Evolution and Stationarity
author_source: Dekimpe, M. G. & Hanssens, D. M., Marketing Science 14(3_supplement), G109-G121, 1995, article
note: Meta-study of unit-root findings across published marketing series: market shares are mostly stationary while many sales series evolve. Supports discussion of why stationarity matters for model choice.
course_use: Background reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: On the Use of Econometric Models for Policy Simulation in Marketing
author_source: Franses, P. H., Journal of Marketing Research 42(1), 4-14, 2005, article
note: Argues that models for policy simulation must account for how marketing instruments themselves are set (endogeneity); illustrated with time-series sales models. Good critical reading on what time-series regressions can support for decisions.
course_use: Critical/methods reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: The Long-Term Effect of Marketing Strategy on Brand Sales
author_source: Ataman, M. B., van Heerde, H. J. & Mela, C. F., Journal of Marketing Research 47(5), 866-882, 2010, article
note: Bayesian dynamic linear (state-space) model of 70 brands in 25 categories over five years (France); long-term elasticities of distribution and line length exceed those of advertising and discounting. Shows a state-space alternative to VAR.
course_use: Application reading (state-space / time-varying parameters); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Discovering How Advertising Grows Sales and Builds Brands
author_source: Bruce, N. I., Peters, K. & Naik, P. A., Journal of Marketing Research 49(6), 793-806, 2012, article
note: Dynamic (Kalman-filter) model linking advertising to brand-building metrics and sales over time; illustrates latent-state time-series modelling and adstock-like carryover.
course_use: Advanced application reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Practice Prize Winner - Dynamic Marketing Budget Allocation Across Countries, Products, and Marketing Activities
author_source: Fischer, M., Albers, S., Wagner, N. & Frie, M., Marketing Science 30(4), 568-585, 2011, article
note: International: dynamic sales-response models with carryover feed a heuristic that allocates a pharma marketing budget across countries, products and activities (Bayer implementation). Shows how estimated time-series response is turned into multi-country budget decisions.
course_use: Core reading for the international angle / case discussion; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: How Business Cycles Contribute to Private-Label Success: Evidence from the United States and Europe
author_source: Lamey, L., Deleersnyder, B., Dekimpe, M. G., Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., Journal of Marketing 71(1), 1-15, 2007, article
note: Long time series of private-label share in the US and three European countries (Belgium, Germany, UK) related to the business cycle with asymmetric (contraction vs expansion) time series models. Key result: private labels gain more in contractions than they lose in expansions, so part of the gain is permanent (ratchet effect).
course_use: Core reading or case for the private-label/retail session; replicate the asymmetric-response idea with dummy-interacted regressions. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The Role of National Culture in Advertising's Sensitivity to Business Cycles: An Investigation Across Continents
author_source: Deleersnyder, B., Dekimpe, M. G., Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., Leeflang, P. S. H., Journal of Marketing Research 46(5), 623-636, 2009, article
note: Advertising expenditure series for 37 countries and four media (magazines, newspapers, radio, TV); extracts cyclical components and relates the cyclical sensitivity of ad spending to Hofstede dimensions, stock-market pressure and foreign MNC presence. Finding: advertising is far more cyclical than GDP; less cyclical in long-term-oriented and high power distance countries, more cyclical under high uncertainty avoidance.
course_use: Core reading; ideal for demonstrating business-cycle filtering of country series followed by a second-stage cross-country regression. Free version via UNC repository; JMR WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Weathering Tight Economic Times: The Sales Evolution of Consumer Durables Over the Business Cycle
author_source: Deleersnyder, B., Dekimpe, M. G., Sarvary, M., Parker, P. M., Quantitative Marketing and Economics 2(4), 347-383, 2004, article
note: Classic on the cyclical sensitivity of consumer durables sales relative to the general economy, using business-cycle filtering and asymmetry tests on long series. Durables are more cyclical than GDP. Caveat: mainly US series; the method transfers to country data.
course_use: Background/methods reading for business-cycle filtering. Working-paper version on KU Leuven Lirias; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Price and Advertising Effectiveness over the Business Cycle
author_source: van Heerde, H. J., Gijsenberg, M. J., Dekimpe, M. G., Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., Journal of Marketing Research 50(2), 177-193, 2013, article
note: Time-varying short- and long-term price and advertising elasticities for 150 brands in 36 CPG categories, 18 years of monthly UK data (1993-2010). Long-term price sensitivity falls in expansions and advertising effectiveness also varies with the economic tide: elasticities are not constant over time.
course_use: Core or advanced reading for the elasticity session; motivates time-varying coefficients beyond static ARIMAX. Open version via RUG repository; JMR WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Do display ads influence search? Attribution and dynamics in online advertising
author_source: Kireyev, P., Pauwels, K. & Gupta, S., International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 475-490, 2016, article
note: Recent VAR application to digital advertising: display ads raise search activity with a lag (cross-channel dynamics and attribution). Persistence/IRF approach on online data; suits digital marketing analytics students.
course_use: Application reading (digital, attribution); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Brand Buzz in the Echoverse
author_source: Hewett, K., Rand, W., Rust, R. T. & van Heerde, H. J., Journal of Marketing 80(3), 1-24, 2016, article
note: VAR on brand communications, traditional media, earned social media (Twitter) and deposits for US banks; shows echo effects and feedback loops, with IRF figures suitable for class discussion.
course_use: Application reading (social media dynamics); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Improving Consumer Mindset Metrics and Shareholder Value through Social Media: The Different Roles of Owned and Earned Media
author_source: Colicev, A., Malshe, A., Pauwels, K. & O'Connor, P., Journal of Marketing 82(1), 37-56, 2018, article
note: Panel VAR of owned and earned social media, YouGov BrandIndex mindset metrics and shareholder value for multiple brands; demonstrates VAR with mindset metrics and long-term effects.
course_use: Application reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Consumer Attitude Metrics for Guiding Marketing Mix Decisions
author_source: Hanssens, D. M., Pauwels, K. H., Srinivasan, S., Vanhuele, M. & Yildirim, G., Marketing Science 33(4), 534-550, 2014, article
note: VAR-based comparison of sales response models with and without attitudinal metrics (awareness, consideration, liking) for brands in France; tests gains in explanatory and forecasting power. Links time-series regression to marketing-mix decisions.
course_use: Application / discussion reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Social Media's Impact on the Consumer Mindset: When to Use Which Sentiment Extraction Tool?
author_source: Kübler, R. V., Colicev, A. & Pauwels, K. H., Journal of Interactive Marketing 50(1), 136-155, 2020, article
note: Compares sentiment-extraction tools as inputs to VAR models of consumer mindset metrics; the choice of text metric changes explanatory and predictive power. Bridges text analytics and time-series modelling.
course_use: Advanced application reading; paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Losses Loom Longer than Gains: Modeling the Impact of Service Crises on Perceived Service Quality over Time
author_source: Gijsenberg, M. J., van Heerde, H. J. & Verhoef, P. C., Journal of Marketing Research 52(5), 642-656, 2015, article
note: Dynamic model of perceived service quality around service crises (Dutch railways); models asymmetric event effects and their decay, a modern take on intervention analysis.
course_use: Application reading (interventions/events); paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen

title: Inferring causal impact using Bayesian structural time-series models
author_source: Brodersen, K. H., Gallusser, F., Koehler, J., Remy, N. & Scott, S. L., Annals of Applied Statistics 9(1), 247-274, 2015, article
note: CausalImpact method (Google): Bayesian structural time series with control series to estimate the effect of a campaign or intervention, illustrated with an online advertising example. The companion R package CausalImpact makes it ideal for a lab; preprint freely available (arXiv/Google Research).
course_use: Lab (campaign intervention effect) + reading; free preprint, journal version paid

title: Another look at measures of forecast accuracy
author_source: Hyndman, R. J. & Koehler, A. B., International Journal of Forecasting 22(4), 679-688, 2006, article
note: Introduces MASE and critiques MAPE/sMAPE; standard reference for choosing accuracy measures when comparing ARIMA vs. regression forecasts across series of different scale (e.g., countries). Short (10 pp.); preprint on the author's website.
course_use: Core reading for forecast evaluation; free preprint on author site, journal paid

title: Automatic Time Series Forecasting: The forecast Package for R
author_source: Hyndman, R. J. & Khandakar, Y., Journal of Statistical Software 27(3), 2008, article
note: Describes the auto.arima and ets algorithms (unit-root testing via KPSS, AICc model selection) underlying the R forecast package; the go-to explanation of automated Box-Jenkins identification for labs.
course_use: Lab companion (R); open access

title: The M4 Competition: 100,000 time series and 61 forecasting methods
author_source: Makridakis, S., Spiliotis, E. & Assimakopoulos, V., International Journal of Forecasting 36(1), 54-74, 2020, article
note: Results of M4: combinations and hybrid statistical/ML methods perform best, pure ML methods underperform; benchmarks include ARIMA, ETS and Theta. Data and code are public on GitHub and usable for forecasting exercises.
course_use: Core reading on forecasting accuracy + lab data; open access

title: M5 accuracy competition: Results, findings, and conclusions
author_source: Spyros Makridakis, Evangelos Spiliotis & Vassilios Assimakopoulos, International Journal of Forecasting 38(4), 2022, report
note: Results of the M5 competition on 42,840 Walmart unit-sales series (hierarchical: item, store, state; with prices, SNAP and calendar events). Compares statistical (ARIMA, ETS) with ML (LightGBM) methods; role of hierarchy and explanatory variables. Data free on Kaggle.
course_use: Case on retail sales forecasting with promotions; students benchmark ARIMA vs. ML on M5 data. Open access (Elsevier).

title: Retail forecasting: Research and practice
author_source: Fildes, R., Ma, S. & Kolassa, S., International Journal of Forecasting 38(4), 1283-1318, 2022, article
note: Review of retail demand forecasting at different hierarchy levels, including promotion effects, regression with ARIMA-type errors and machine learning; links practice and research. Good bridge from sales response modelling to forecasting.
course_use: Background reading; open access status to check, journal

title: Forecasting: theory and practice
author_source: Petropoulos, F. et al. (80+ authors), International Journal of Forecasting 38(3), 705-871, 2022, article
note: Encyclopedic review with short self-contained sections (ARIMA, exponential smoothing, interventions, forecast combination, evaluation, marketing and retail applications). Instructors can assign individual 1-2 page sections.
course_use: Reference / selective reading; open access

title: Marketing Budget Allocation Across Countries: The Role of International Business Cycles
author_source: Peers, Y., van Heerde, H. J., Dekimpe, M. G., Marketing Science 36(5), 792-809, 2017, article
note: Directly on topic: how to allocate a marketing budget across origin countries whose business cycles are not synchronised, illustrated with tourism marketing (tourists from several origin countries). Separates whether unit sales, marketing effectiveness and margins move pro- or countercyclically per country. Good bridge between time series regression with cyclical components and an international budgeting decision.
course_use: Core reading for the international session; case discussion on pro- vs countercyclical spending. Open-access version via EUR repository; publisher version WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The Effect of Business-Cycle Fluctuations on Private-Label Share: What has Marketing Conduct Got to do with it?
author_source: Lamey, L., Deleersnyder, B., Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., Dekimpe, M. G., Journal of Marketing 76(1), 1-19, 2012, article
note: Follow-up to Lamey et al. (2007): two decades of data on 106 US CPG categories with seven marketing-mix instruments. Private-label share is countercyclical and partly permanently boosted; national brands' procyclical cuts in advertising, promotions and new product introductions amplify this. Caveat: US only, so pair it with the 2007 multi-country paper.
course_use: Supplementary reading; good for discussing marketing conduct as a mediator in time series. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Business cycle research in marketing: a review and research agenda
author_source: Dekimpe, M. G., Deleersnyder, B., Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science 46(1), 31-58, 2018, article
note: Review of marketing research on business cycles: cyclical filtering methods, asymmetric effects and multi-country evidence (advertising, private labels, durables, marketing effectiveness). Useful map of the Dekimpe/Steenkamp/Deleersnyder research stream for students.
course_use: Background reading at the start of the international/macro session. Open access.

title: The Impact of Economic Contractions on the Effectiveness of R&D and Advertising: Evidence from U.S. Companies Spanning Three Decades
author_source: Steenkamp, J.-B. E. M., Fang, E., Marketing Science 30(4), 628-645, 2011, article
note: Firm panel over three decades showing that advertising and R&D investments pay off more (profit, market share) during contractions. US-only, but a standard reference in the countercyclical-spending debate; useful contrast to Deleersnyder et al. (2009).
course_use: Background reading / discussion input for the business-cycle debate. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The International Takeoff of New Products: The Role of Economics, Culture, and Country Innovativeness
author_source: Tellis, G. J., Stremersch, S., Yin, E., Marketing Science 22(2), 188-208, 2003, article
note: Sales time series of ten consumer durables across 16 European countries; identifies takeoff from the sales curve and models time to takeoff with a hazard model. Takeoff timing differs strongly across countries (Scandinavian fast, Mediterranean slower) and relates to culture and economics; discusses waterfall vs sprinkler entry.
course_use: Core reading for international diffusion; exercise: identify takeoff points in country sales series. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Understanding and managing international growth of new products
author_source: Stremersch, S., Tellis, G. J., International Journal of Research in Marketing 21(4), 421-438, 2004, article
note: Companion to the takeoff paper: studies the growth stage (duration and growth rate after takeoff) of new products across European countries; economic factors explain cross-country growth differences better than culture.
course_use: Supplementary reading alongside Tellis et al. (2003). Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Global Takeoff of New Products: Culture, Wealth, or Vanishing Differences?
author_source: Chandrasekaran, D., Tellis, G. J., Marketing Science 27(5), 844-860, 2008, article
note: 16 products in 31 developed and developing countries (430 categories), parametric hazard model of time to takeoff with 12 drivers. Fastest takeoff in Japan and Norway; culture and wealth matter; time to takeoff shortens over calendar time and converges across countries.
course_use: Core reading for emerging vs developed market diffusion; good class debate on convergence. SSRN version free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Modeling Global Spillover of New Product Takeoff
author_source: van Everdingen, Y., Fok, D., Stremersch, S., Journal of Marketing Research 46(5), 637-652, 2009, article
note: Penetration data for eight high-tech products across 55 countries; foreign takeoffs (not mere introductions) accelerate a focal country's takeoff. Large, wealthy, export-heavy countries have more clout; poorer, tourist-receiving, densely populated countries are more susceptible; spillovers are stronger between geographically and economically close countries.
course_use: Core or supplementary reading on cross-country dependence in time series. SSRN version free; JMR WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Global Diffusion of Technological Innovations: A Coupled-Hazard Approach
author_source: Dekimpe, M. G., Parker, P. M., Sarvary, M., Journal of Marketing Research 37(1), 47-59, 2000, article
note: Classic on global diffusion of cellular telephony across a very large set of countries, modelling country-level adoption timing and diffusion with a coupled-hazard model and country covariates. Shows how international diffusion data are structured and why country heterogeneity matters.
course_use: Background classic for the diffusion block. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Investigating New Product Diffusion Across Products and Countries
author_source: Talukdar, D., Sudhir, K., Ainslie, A., Marketing Science 21(1), 97-114, 2002, article
note: Hierarchical Bayesian Bass model for several products across developed and developing countries; developing countries show lower penetration potential and slower diffusion; pooling across countries improves early forecasts.
course_use: Core reading for forecasting diffusion in emerging markets; lab: fit Bass curves per country. Open access per OpenAlex; otherwise WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Social Contagion and Income Heterogeneity in New Product Diffusion: A Meta-Analytic Test
author_source: Van den Bulte, C., Stremersch, S., Marketing Science 23(4), 530-544, 2004, article
note: Meta-analysis of Bass model parameters (q/p ratio) from many studies across countries; relates cross-country differences to income inequality and Hofstede culture dimensions. Useful for interpreting Bass parameters in international comparisons.
course_use: Supplementary reading for diffusion; source of benchmark parameters. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Innovation diffusion and new product growth models: A critical review and research directions
author_source: Peres, R., Muller, E., Mahajan, V., International Journal of Research in Marketing 27(2), 91-106, 2010, article
note: Review of diffusion and growth models including cross-country diffusion, international spillovers, takeoff and saddles. Good overview before the empirical takeoff papers.
course_use: Background reading for the diffusion block. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Functional Regression: A New Model for Predicting Market Penetration of New Products
author_source: Sood, A., James, G. M., Tellis, G. J., Marketing Science 28(1), 36-51, 2009, article
note: Penetration curves of 760 categories (21 products x 70 countries); compares functional regression with Classic Bass, Meta-Bass and naive benchmarks for predicting eight aspects of penetration. Augmented functional regression forecasts best; product effects matter more than country effects. Strong example of global demand forecasting with out-of-sample evaluation.
course_use: Advanced reading / forecasting benchmark discussion. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Marketing mix and brand sales in global markets: Examining the contingent role of country-market characteristics
author_source: Bahadir, S. C., Bharadwaj, S. G., Srivastava, R. K., Journal of International Business Studies 46(5), 596-619, 2015, article
note: Estimates marketing-mix elasticities for brands across many country markets from longitudinal sales data and explains how elasticities vary with country-market characteristics (e.g. economic development, culture). Relevant for emerging vs developed market comparisons. Check details of instruments and country sample before assigning.
course_use: Core reading for cross-country elasticity comparisons. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Winning hearts, minds and sales: How marketing communication enters the purchase process in emerging and mature markets
author_source: Pauwels, K., Erguncu, S., Yildirim, G., International Journal of Research in Marketing 30(1), 57-68, 2013, article
note: Vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling of marketing communication, consumer mindset metrics and sales, contrasting an emerging and a mature market; impulse responses show how communication moves through awareness, consideration and liking to sales differently across market types.
course_use: Core reading for the VAR/impulse-response lab with an international angle. SSRN version free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: New Empirical Generalizations on the Determinants of Price Elasticity
author_source: Bijmolt, T. H. A., van Heerde, H. J., Pieters, R. G. M., Journal of Marketing Research 42(2), 141-156, 2005, article
note: Meta-analysis of about 1,850 price elasticities (mean about -2.6) with moderators including country/region, time period, data aggregation and estimation method; documents that price elasticities changed over time.
course_use: Benchmark reading for price elasticity labs. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: How cannibalistic is the Internet channel? A study of the newspaper industry in the United Kingdom and the Netherlands
author_source: Deleersnyder, B., Geyskens, I., Gielens, K., Dekimpe, M. G., International Journal of Research in Marketing 19(4), 337-348, 2002, article
note: Intervention/structural-break time series analysis of newspaper circulation and advertising around the launch of online editions in the UK and the Netherlands; cannibalisation was rarer than feared. Clean two-country example of intervention analysis.
course_use: Lab example for intervention analysis and structural breaks. Open access per OpenAlex.

title: Exchange rate pass-through for strategic pricing and advertising
author_source: Kadiyali, V., Journal of International Economics 43(3-4), 437-461, 1997, article
note: Marketing-relevant exchange-rate pass-through study (US photographic film market, Kodak vs Fuji): estimates pass-through into both price and advertising in a structural NEIO model; incomplete pass-through depends on demand, cost and competitive conduct.
course_use: Background reading on exchange rates and international pricing/advertising. Open access per OpenAlex.

title: Currency Choice and Exchange Rate Pass-Through
author_source: Gopinath, G., Itskhoki, O., Rigobon, R., American Economic Review 100(1), 304-336, 2010, article
note: Micro data on US import prices show that pass-through depends strongly on invoicing currency (dollar vs non-dollar priced goods), in the short and the long run. Explains why export prices and sales react differently across markets after exchange-rate shocks.
course_use: Background reading for export pricing; economics-heavy, assign selected sections. Open access per OpenAlex.

title: Pricing-to-Market: Evidence From Plant-Level Prices
author_source: Fitzgerald, D., Haller, S., Review of Economic Studies 81(2), 761-786, 2014, article
note: Monthly plant-level prices of Irish producers selling the same product in Ireland and the UK. With local-currency invoicing, the relative markup moves one-for-one with exchange-rate changes: direct evidence of pricing-to-market. Intuitive case for international price-setting over time.
course_use: Case discussion on export pricing and exchange rates. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Tourism demand modelling and forecasting - A review of recent research
author_source: Song, H., Li, G., Tourism Management 29(2), 203-220, 2008, article
note: Review of international tourism demand forecasting (ARIMA, exponential smoothing, ADL/ECM, VAR, time-varying parameter models) with accuracy comparisons; no single method dominates across origin-destination pairs.
course_use: Background reading for the tourism forecasting lab. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A review of research on tourism demand forecasting: Launching the Annals of Tourism Research Curated Collection on tourism demand forecasting
author_source: Song, H., Qiu, R. T. R., Park, J., Annals of Tourism Research 75, 338-362, 2019, article
note: Updated review of more than 200 tourism demand forecasting studies: time series (ARIMA/SARIMA, ETS), econometric and AI models, forecast combination and search-engine data, plus accuracy measures and research design.
course_use: Background reading. Open access.

title: The tourism forecasting competition
author_source: Athanasopoulos, G., Hyndman, R. J., Song, H., Wu, D. C., International Journal of Forecasting 27(3), 822-844, 2011, article
note: Forecasting competition on 1,311 monthly, quarterly and annual tourism series: compares ARIMA, ETS, damped trend, naive and econometric models. Naive forecasts are hard to beat for annual data; automated ETS/ARIMA do well for monthly and quarterly data. Competition data are public (R package Tcomp).
course_use: Core reading plus lab: reuse the competition data to benchmark ARIMA vs ETS. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen; data free.

title: Time series forecasts of international travel demand for Australia
author_source: Lim, C., McAleer, M., Tourism Management 23(4), 389-396, 2002, article
note: Short classic applying Box-Jenkins ARIMA/seasonal ARIMA to quarterly tourist arrivals to Australia from Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore, with unit-root testing and accuracy comparison. Easy to replicate step by step.
course_use: Lab template for a seasonal ARIMA exercise. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Forecasting tourism demand with Google trends: Accuracy comparison of countries versus cities
author_source: Önder, I., International Journal of Tourism Research 19(6), 648-660, 2017, article
note: Compares autoregressive baselines with models adding Google Trends web and image search indices for Vienna, Barcelona, Austria and Belgium; search indices help most for Vienna. Direct local relevance for a WU audience.
course_use: Lab idea: replicate with Google Trends data for Austria/Vienna and Statistik Austria arrivals. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Can Google data improve the forecasting performance of tourist arrivals? Mixed-data sampling approach
author_source: Bangwayo-Skeete, P. F., Skeete, R. W., Tourism Management 46, 454-464, 2015, article
note: Uses weekly Google search data in MIDAS models to forecast monthly tourist arrivals to Caribbean destinations from major origin markets, against SARIMA and AR benchmarks; Google-augmented MIDAS improves accuracy in most cases.
course_use: Supplementary reading for mixed-frequency nowcasting. Paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Predicting the Present with Google Trends
author_source: Choi, H., Varian, H., Economic Record 88(s1), 2-9, 2012, article
note: Short foundational paper: adds Google Trends query indices to simple seasonal AR models to nowcast retail sales, car sales, unemployment claims, travel (visitor arrivals to Hong Kong by origin country) and consumer confidence. Very accessible ARIMAX-type example.
course_use: Core short reading and lab starter for Google Trends nowcasting. Journal paid (WU-Lizenz prüfen); earlier Google preprint version freely circulated.

title: Forecasting GDP growth rates in the United States and Brazil using Google Trends
author_source: Bantis, E., Clements, M. P., Urquhart, A., International Journal of Forecasting 39(4), 1909-1924, 2023, article
note: Dynamic factor models with Google Trends categories to nowcast GDP in a developed (US) and an emerging (Brazil) economy, handling the ragged-edge problem. Gains are broadly similar in both countries; more disaggregated queries do not help. Useful for cross-country nowcasting design choices.
course_use: Advanced reading on nowcasting across countries. Open access.

title: Forecasting tourism recovery amid COVID-19
author_source: Zhang, H., Song, H., Wen, L., Liu, C., Annals of Tourism Research 87, 103149, 2021, article
note: Forecasts the recovery of inbound tourism to Hong Kong from major source markets after the COVID-19 shock, combining econometric/time series forecasts with scenario analysis and expert judgmental adjustment. Shows how to forecast when a structural break invalidates history.
course_use: Case discussion: forecasting under shocks and structural breaks. Open access.

title: Visitor arrivals forecasts amid COVID-19: A perspective from the Europe team
author_source: Liu, A., Vici, L., Ramos, V., Giannoni, S., Blake, A., Annals of Tourism Research 88, 103182, 2021, article
note: Contribution to an international forecasting challenge on COVID-19 recovery: forecasts visitor arrivals to European destinations with time series/econometric models combined with scenario-based judgment.
course_use: Supplementary case for European international arrivals under shocks. Preprint free on HAL.

title: Back to Trend: COVID Effects on E-commerce in 47 Countries
author_source: Alcedo, J., Cavallo, A., Dwyer, B., Mishra, P., Spilimbergo, A., NBER Working Paper 29729, 2022, working paper
note: Mastercard transaction data for 47 economies and 26 industries before, during and after COVID-19. Online shares surged with lockdowns and fiscal transfers, then returned to pre-pandemic trends in almost all countries: little evidence of permanent structural change. Ideal multi-country example of temporary vs permanent shocks (link to persistence modelling).
course_use: Case discussion / intervention analysis exercise. Free (NBER).

title: Estimation of Panel Vector Autoregression in Stata
author_source: Abrigo, M. R. M., Love, I., Stata Journal 16(3), 778-804, 2016, article
note: Practical guide to panel VAR estimation (GMM), lag selection, Granger causality, impulse responses and variance decomposition with the pvar package. Directly usable for multi-country panel time series of marketing or trade data.
course_use: Lab/methods reading for panel VAR with country panels. Open access per OpenAlex.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.)
author_source: Rob J Hyndman & George Athanasopoulos, OTexts, 3rd ed., 2021, book
note: Core course text. Ch. 2-3 graphics/decomposition (STL, X-11, SEATS), Ch. 5 toolbox (residual diagnostics, accuracy), Ch. 7 time series regression (trend, seasonal dummies, Fourier terms, intervention dummies), Ch. 9 ARIMA (stationarity, differencing, ACF/PACF, seasonal ARIMA), Ch. 10 dynamic regression (regression with ARIMA errors, lagged predictors, e.g. advertising-sales), Ch. 11 hierarchical/grouped forecasts (useful for country x product hierarchies). R code (fable/tsibble) and datasets in tsibbledata/fpp3 packages. Master level, non-technical.
course_use: Primary reading for sessions on regression and ARIMA; assign Ch. 7, 9, 10 plus exercises. Free online (print version paid).

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice, the Pythonic Way
author_source: Rob J Hyndman, George Athanasopoulos, Azul Garza, Cristian Challu, Max Mergenthaler, Kin G Olivares, OTexts, online edition (continuously updated, 2025/2026), book
note: Python edition of FPP3 built on the Nixtla open-source stack (statsforecast, mlforecast etc.). Same chapter logic (regression, ARIMA, dynamic regression), so students can choose R or Python.
course_use: Offer as Python alternative to FPP3 for students who code in Python. Free online.

title: Time Series Analysis and Its Applications: With R Examples (5th ed.)
author_source: Robert H. Shumway & David S. Stoffer, Springer Texts in Statistics, 5th ed., 2025, book
note: More rigorous than FPP3. Ch. 1-3 characteristics of time series, regression and exploratory analysis, ARIMA models (estimation, forecasting, seasonal ARIMA, regression with autocorrelated errors); later chapters on spectral analysis and state space models. R code for every example (astsa package). 5th ed. adds changepoints and more structural models.
course_use: Reference for students wanting the statistical foundations; selected chapters for advanced sessions. Paid (~EUR 140-160); WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink). Easier sibling: Time Series: A Data Analysis Approach Using R (CRC 2019).

title: Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control (5th ed.)
author_source: George E. P. Box, Gwilym M. Jenkins, Gregory C. Reinsel & Greta M. Ljung, Wiley, 5th ed., 2015, book
note: The classic origin of the Box-Jenkins ARIMA methodology: identification (ACF/PACF), estimation, diagnostic checking, seasonal models, transfer function and intervention models that underlie advertising-sales and promotion impact analysis.
course_use: Background reference; cite for the Box-Jenkins cycle and transfer-function/intervention analysis. Paid (~EUR 120); check WU library.

title: Applied Econometric Time Series (4th ed.)
author_source: Walter Enders, Wiley, 4th ed., 2015, book
note: Applied econometrics view: Ch. 2 stationary ARMA models (Box-Jenkins, AIC/BIC), Ch. 4 trends and unit roots (Dickey-Fuller), Ch. 5 multiequation models (intervention, transfer functions, VAR, impulse responses), Ch. 6 cointegration. Bridges ARIMA to the VAR/persistence modeling used in marketing.
course_use: Recommended for sessions on unit roots, VAR and persistence modeling. Paid (~EUR 90-120); check WU library. Data sets on author website.

title: Introductory Econometrics: A Modern Approach (7th ed.)
author_source: Jeffrey M. Wooldridge, Cengage, 7th ed., 2020, book
note: Time series chapters: Ch. 10 basic regression with time series data (static and finite distributed lag models, trends, seasonality), Ch. 11 further issues (stationarity, weak dependence, unit roots), Ch. 12 serial correlation and heteroskedasticity (tests, Prais-Winsten, HAC SEs), Ch. 18 advanced topics (infinite distributed lags/Koyck, cointegration, forecasting). Well suited for distributed-lag advertising models.
course_use: Use Ch. 10-12 as bridge from OLS to time series regression. Paid; WU library copies prüfen. Data via wooldridge R/Python packages (free).

title: Introduction to Time Series and Forecasting (3rd ed.)
author_source: Peter J. Brockwell & Richard A. Davis, Springer Texts in Statistics, 3rd ed., 2016, book
note: Concise, mathematically clean intro: stationary processes, ARMA models, modeling and forecasting with ARMA, nonstationary and seasonal ARIMA, multivariate series, state-space models.
course_use: Theory reference for stronger students. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Time Series Models for Business and Economic Forecasting (3rd ed.)
author_source: Philip Hans Franses, Dick van Dijk & Anne Opschoor, Cambridge University Press, 3rd ed., 2014, book
note: Business-oriented forecasting text by Erasmus econometricians (Franses also published widely on marketing time series): trends, seasonality, ARIMA, unit roots, multivariate models, with business examples and exercises.
course_use: Intermediate alternative to Enders with business focus. Paid; check Cambridge Core via WU. DOI to be verified.

title: Market Response Models: Econometric and Time Series Analysis (2nd ed.)
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens, Leonard J. Parsons & Randall L. Schultz, Kluwer/Springer, International Series in Quantitative Marketing, 2nd ed., 2001, book
note: The key marketing reference: sales response functions, carryover/distributed lags (Koyck, Nerlove-Arrow), ARIMA and transfer-function models, Granger causality, VAR and persistence modeling of marketing effects, competitive reaction; empirical generalisations on advertising and price elasticities.
course_use: Core marketing-specific reading linking time series methods to marketing-mix decisions. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Modeling Markets: Analyzing Marketing Phenomena and Improving Marketing Decision Making
author_source: Peter S. H. Leeflang, Jaap E. Wieringa, Tammo H. A. Bijmolt & Koen H. Pauwels, Springer, International Series in Quantitative Marketing, 2015, book
note: Modern marketing-models textbook: specification of response models, dynamic effects (lag structures, carryover), estimation and validation of aggregate models with time series data; many marketing-mix examples. Master/PhD level.
course_use: Use dynamic-model and estimation chapters to show regression with lags in marketing-mix models. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Advanced Methods for Modeling Markets
author_source: Peter S. H. Leeflang, Jaap E. Wieringa, Tammo H. A. Bijmolt & Koen H. Pauwels (eds.), Springer, International Series in Quantitative Marketing, 2017, book
note: Companion to Modeling Markets. Chapter 'Traditional Time Series' (ARIMA, transfer functions, unit roots, VAR/VEC, impulse responses, persistence) and chapter 'State Space Models' are directly relevant; further chapters on diffusion, competition and structural models.
course_use: Key reading for VAR/persistence and state space models in marketing. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Long-Term Impact of Marketing: A Compendium
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens (ed.), World Scientific, 2018, book
note: Four decades of Hanssens and coauthors' time-series marketing research: market response and competitive behaviour (Ch. 1), persistence modeling, long-run advertising and price effects, marketing and firm value (Ch. 12, Srinivasan & Hanssens). Applied VAR, unit-root and persistence models on real marketing data.
course_use: Source of exemplary applied papers for advanced sessions and student projects. Paid (~USD 180); check WU library.

title: Handbook of Marketing Decision Models (2nd ed.) - chapter Time-Series Models in Marketing
author_source: Berend Wierenga & Ralf van der Lans (eds.), Springer, 2017 (1st ed. 2008; chapter by Dekimpe, Franses, Hanssens & Naik), book
note: Chapter 'Time-Series Models in Marketing' (1st ed.: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-78213-3_11) surveys unit roots, VAR, persistence and state space models with marketing examples. Concise overview ideal for master students.
course_use: Assign the time series chapter as overview reading. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Handbook of Market Research - chapter Modeling Marketing Dynamics Using Vector Autoregressive (VAR) Models
author_source: Shuba Srinivasan, in: C. Homburg, M. Klarmann & A. Vomberg (eds.), Handbook of Market Research, Springer, 2022, book chapter
note: Tutorial chapter on VAR modeling in marketing: unit-root testing, VAR/VEC specification, Granger causality, impulse response functions, forecast error variance decomposition, with application.
course_use: Hands-on reading for a VAR/persistence session. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Principles of Business Forecasting (2nd ed.)
author_source: Keith Ord, Robert Fildes & Nikolaos Kourentzes, Wessex Press, 2nd ed., 2017, book
note: Managerial forecasting textbook: exponential smoothing, ARIMA, regression for forecasting incl. promotions and causal variables, judgmental forecasting, forecasting in organisations; sales/marketing examples.
course_use: Complement for managerial framing (forecast process, accuracy). Paid (~USD 100).

title: It's Not the Size of the Data - It's How You Use It: Smarter Marketing with Analytics and Dashboards
author_source: Koen Pauwels, AMACOM, 2014, book
note: Practitioner book by a leading VAR-in-marketing researcher: marketing dashboards, leading indicators, using time series (VAR, Granger causality) to link marketing actions to sales; international company cases.
course_use: Non-technical motivation reading; good for cases and discussion. Paid (~EUR 25).

title: Introduction to Modern Time Series Analysis (2nd ed.)
author_source: Gebhard Kirchgässner, Jürgen Wolters & Uwe Hassler, Springer Texts in Business and Economics, 2nd ed., 2013, book
note: Compact econometric intro: univariate ARMA/ARIMA, Granger causality, VAR, unit roots and cointegration, ARCH. English version of the German classic Einführung in die moderne Zeitreihenanalyse (Kirchgässner/Wolters, Vahlen 2006).
course_use: Short, rigorous companion for VAR/cointegration. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Zeitreihenanalyse in den Wirtschaftswissenschaften (3. Aufl.)
author_source: Klaus Neusser, Vieweg+Teubner/Springer, 3. Aufl., 2011, book (German)
note: Deutschsprachiges Lehrbuch: ARMA-Modelle, Schätzung und Prognose, Box-Jenkins, Einheitswurzeltests, VAR, Kointegration, Zustandsraummodelle. English version: Time Series Econometrics, Springer 2016 (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-32862-1).
course_use: German-language reference. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Angewandte Zeitreihenanalyse mit R
author_source: Rainer Schlittgen & Cristina Sattarhoff, De Gruyter Oldenbourg, 4. Aufl., 2020 (1. Aufl. 2010/2012), book (German)
note: Anwendungsorientiertes deutsches Lehrbuch mit R: Trend- und Saisonbereinigung, ARMA/ARIMA, Regression mit Zeitreihen, Interventionsanalyse, Transferfunktionen, multivariate Modelle; viele Beispiele mit R-Code. Classic theory counterpart: Schlittgen & Streitberg, Zeitreihenanalyse (https://doi.org/10.1524/9783486710960).
course_use: German applied companion with R code. Paid (~EUR 50); check WU library / De Gruyter licence; current edition details to be verified.

title: Modelle der Zeitreihenanalyse
author_source: Manfred Deistler & Wolfgang Scherrer, Birkhäuser/Springer, 2018, book (German)
note: Theoretical German text by TU Wien authors (Austrian link): stationary processes, ARMA and state space systems, prediction, estimation, multivariate models. Mathematically demanding.
course_use: For mathematically interested students only. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Multivariate Analysemethoden - Kapitel Zeitreihenanalyse
author_source: Klaus Backhaus, Bernd Erichson, Wulff Plinke & Rolf Weiber, Springer Gabler, 15. Aufl., 2018 (newer editions available), book chapter (German)
note: Standard German marketing-research methods book; chapter Zeitreihenanalyse introduces trend/seasonal regression, autocorrelation, ARIMA and forecasting with a sales example and SPSS. Very accessible.
course_use: Easy German entry chapter widely known among WU students; use the latest edition. WU-Lizenz prüfen (SpringerLink).

title: Empirical Generalizations about Marketing Impact (2nd ed.)
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens (ed.), Marketing Science Institute, Relevant Knowledge Series, 2015, book
note: Compact compendium of benchmarks: advertising, price and promotion elasticities, short- vs. long-run effects, carryover, diffusion; largely derived from time series models across many countries and categories.
course_use: Benchmarks to compare students' estimated elasticities; discussion of cross-country generalisability. MSI publication (members/paid); exact URL to be verified.

title: The M6 forecasting competition: Bridging the gap between forecasting and investment decisions
author_source: Spyros Makridakis, Evangelos Spiliotis, Ross Hollyman, Fotios Petropoulos, Norman Swanson & Anil Gaba, International Journal of Forecasting 41(4), 2025, report
note: Live competition (Feb 2022-Feb 2023, 100 assets): hard to beat the market; weak link between forecasts and decisions; value of information sharing. Data and submissions on GitHub.
course_use: Optional reading on limits of forecastability and the forecast-decision link; less marketing-specific than M5. Check journal for OA status.

title: X-13ARIMA-SEATS Seasonal Adjustment Program (software, reference manual, utilities)
author_source: U.S. Census Bureau, page revised July 2025, report/manual
note: Official home of X-13ARIMA-SEATS: regARIMA (regression with ARIMA errors), X-11 and SEATS adjustment, trading-day and moving-holiday regressors (Win Genhol for user-defined holidays such as Chinese New Year), diagnostics, batch processing. Usable from R via the seasonal package.
course_use: Explain how official statistics adjust monthly sales series and how holiday effects differ across countries. Free.

title: ESS Guidelines on Seasonal Adjustment - 2024 edition
author_source: Eurostat, Manuals and Guidelines KS-GQ-24-012, 2024, report
note: European standard for seasonal and calendar adjustment (doi 10.2785/705102): pre-treatment (outliers, national calendar effects), X-13 vs TRAMO-SEATS, revisions; new sections on high-frequency data, shocks (COVID) and long series. Recommends JDemetra+.
course_use: Selected sections when discussing seasonality and calendar effects in cross-country EU data. Free PDF.

title: Seasonal adjustment - Trusted Smart Statistics: JDemetra+ and RJDemetra (2024 training)
author_source: Eurostat CROS portal (JDemetra+ developed by National Bank of Belgium with Deutsche Bundesbank and Eurostat), 2024, report/training material
note: Training material for JDemetra+ (ESS-recommended since 2015, free, open source, EUPL) and its R interface RJDemetra: X-13 and TRAMO-SEATS in practice.
course_use: Shows the tool chain of European statistical offices (ESS members incl. Statistik Austria). Free.

title: Saisonbereinigung der Konjunkturstatistiken mit X-12-ARIMA und mit X13 in JDemetra+
author_source: Stefan Linz, Claudia Fries & Julia Völker, Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis), WISTA 4/2018, S. 59-80, report (German)
note: Deutschsprachige Methodenbeschreibung: Vergleich X-12-ARIMA vs. X13 in JDemetra+, Kalenderbereinigung, Ausreißer, Revisionen. No Statistik Austria methodology document surfaced in this search; check statistik.at directly.
course_use: German-language reading on seasonal adjustment in official statistics. Free PDF.

author_source: International Monetary Fund, 2018, report

title: Forecasting at Scale (Prophet)
author_source: Sean J. Taylor & Benjamin Letham (Facebook), The American Statistician 72(1), 37-45, 2018 (PeerJ Preprint 2017), white paper

title: Bayesian Methods for Media Mix Modeling with Carryover and Shape Effects
author_source: Yuxue Jin, Yueqing Wang, Yunting Sun, David Chan & Jim Koehler, Google Inc., 2017, white paper

course_use: Read when moving from distributed-lag regression to modern MMM. Free.

title: The Long and the Short of It: Balancing Short and Long-Term Marketing Strategies
author_source: Les Binet & Peter Field, Institute of Practitioners in Advertising (IPA), 2013, report
note: Analysis of the IPA Databank (effectiveness cases from many countries): short-term activation vs. long-term brand building, 60:40 heuristic. Not econometrics itself, but motivates long-term effect measurement addressed by persistence/VAR models.
course_use: Discussion reading on short- vs. long-run effects; contrast with econometric evidence (Hanssens). Paid for non-members (IPA shop).

title: The Multiplier Effect (and Ebiquity/WARC: The long-term impact of advertising)
author_source: WARC with Analytic Partners, BERA.ai, Prophet & System1, 2025; Ebiquity study on WARC 2018, report
note: Industry evidence that brand equity multiplies short-term returns; Ebiquity study of 504 campaigns/29 advertisers estimated long-term multipliers by medium (TV about 2.4). Based on econometric MMM across markets.
course_use: Practitioner evidence for long-term effects; use critically (limited method transparency). Registration required; full WARC content needs subscription (check WU access).

title: MSI Research Priorities 2024-2026
author_source: Marketing Science Institute, 2024, report
note: Research agenda of the Marketing Science Institute incl. measuring marketing effectiveness, long-term effects, AI and analytics. Shows academic relevance and thesis topics.
course_use: Short reading to motivate thesis topics. Free (registration may be needed). Old priorities URL returned 404; exact page to be verified.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed), Chapter 10 Dynamic regression models
author_source: Rob J Hyndman & George Athanasopoulos, OTexts, 2021 (online edition), open textbook website, English
note: Regression with ARIMA errors in R (fable): estimation, forecasting, stochastic vs deterministic trends, dynamic harmonic regression, lagged predictors. Section 10.6 models monthly insurance quotations on TV advertising with lags up to 3 months - a ready-made advertising-carryover example; 10.2 US consumption vs income; 10.5 Australian eating-out turnover. Chapter 9 (ARIMA) precedes it. Master level, exercises included; embedded videos in many sections.
course_use: Core reading/lab companion for the R track; assign 10.6 as the advertising-lag case. Free, open access.

title: statsmodels SARIMAX API reference and 'SARIMAX: Introduction' notebook

author_source: Irem Önder, Ulrich Gunter (MODUL University Vienna); Tourism Analysis 21(2-3), 2016, journal article

title: Now- und Forecasting touristischer Nächtigungen, Umsätze und Wertschöpfung für Österreich
author_source: Oliver Fritz, Anna Burton, Philipp Piribauer; WIFO Studies 69823, 2022, commissioned by Österreich Werbung

course_use: Austrian real-world example of model competition and forecast evaluation; discuss it with an ARIMA lab on Austrian tourism data. Free.

title: Statistik Austria: Ankünfte und Nächtigungen (monthly tourism statistics, e.g. December 2025 release)
author_source: Statistik Austria, press release and monthly tourism statistics, 2026
note: Monthly arrivals and overnight stays by federal state and origin country. Vienna passed 20 million nights in 2025 (+6.5%), and about 74% of all nights were foreign guests (Germany, Netherlands, Switzerland). Long series are available in STATcube.
course_use: Data source for a SARIMA lab on Vienna nights by origin market, including the COVID intervention (2020-2021). Free.

title: Forecasting the Evolving Composition of Inbound Tourism Demand: A Bayesian Compositional Time Series Approach Using Platform Booking Data
author_source: Harrison Katz (Airbnb); arXiv 2602.18358, 2026, preprint
note: Forecasts guest-origin-market shares for four destination regions with BDARMA on Airbnb data from 2017 to 2025. Benchmarks are naive, ETS and SARIMA on log-ratios. It shows pandemic breaks with uneven recovery by market; about 27% lower error than naive for EMEA. Proprietary data.
course_use: Advanced example of forecasting country-of-origin mix, a core international-marketing question; students replicate the idea with Statistik Austria nights by origin. Free.

title: Deep Learning based Forecasting: a case study from the online fashion industry (Zalando)
author_source: Manuel Kunz, Stefan Birr, Tim Januschowski et al. (Zalando); arXiv 2305.14406, 2023, preprint
note: Zalando's global, transformer-based demand forecasting for a fashion catalogue with high turnover. It stresses price-demand control under a fixed-inventory assumption. Zalando operates in about 25 European markets. Related 2026 paper: transformer for regular weeks, LightGBM for sales events.
course_use: Discussion: why European e-commerce leaders move from per-series ARIMA to global models, and what ARIMA still offers (interpretability, baselines). Free.

title: SPAR Österreich: KI-Prognose für Obst und Gemüse gegen Lebensmittelverschwendung
author_source: Trending Topics (news), 25 Aug 2022; SPAR Österreich with Microsoft
note: SPAR forecasts per-store order quantities for over 1,500 stores using sales, weather, promotions, marketing campaigns and seasonality. It claims over 90% accuracy (company figure, unverified). It builds on SPAR's long-running automatic ordering system.
course_use: Austrian warm-up example for regressors in demand forecasts (weather, promotions); possible guest speaker from SPAR ICS. Free (German).

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners: Predicting the weather's impact on demand
author_source: Smith Institute, case study (consultancy), ongoing since 2018
note: For CCEP across 31 countries in Europe, Oceania and Southeast Asia, ML models separate weather and public-holiday effects from underlying sales. Weekly weather-based forecasts are used to time marketing and promotions. No quantified results are given (placeholders on the page).
course_use: Example of regression with weather and holiday covariates across countries; students build temperature-adjusted beverage sales models. Free.

title: Unilever demand sensing with Terra Technology (vendor case study)
author_source: IoT ONE case-study listing, based on Terra Technology (now E2open) material, vendor case
note: Reports that 7-day MAPE improved by 22% and European inventory fell by 35% with short-term demand sensing. P&G reported over 50% lower short-horizon error with the same vendor. These are vendor claims without baselines, so treat them critically.
course_use: Critical-reading exercise: what counts as forecast improvement (horizon, baseline, metric)? Free.

title: Predicting the Present with Google Trends
author_source: Hyunyoung Choi, Hal Varian; Google Research blog 2009; Economic Record 88 (special issue), 2012
note: Seasonal AR models of auto sales, home sales, retail sales and travel (Hong Kong visitor arrivals by origin country) improve when Google Trends categories are added. A replication by Coupé (Economics E-Journal 2018) exists.
course_use: Replicate: an AR(1) plus Google Trends nowcast for car registrations or retail sales in Austria or another country; compare out-of-sample MAE. Free.

title: OECD Weekly Tracker of Economic Activity (Google Trends nowcast, 46 countries)
author_source: Nicolas Woloszko, OECD Economics Department Working Paper No. 1634 (2020), OECD data tool
note: A machine-learning nowcast of weekly GDP growth for 46 OECD and G20 countries from Google Trends (consumption, labour, housing, trade, uncertainty), designed for rapid shocks such as COVID. Publication is currently paused for revision.
course_use: Cross-country example of search-data nowcasting; discuss comparability of Google Trends across languages. Free.

title: Google COVID-19 Community Mobility Reports (via Our World in Data)
author_source: Google (2020-2022), processed by Our World in Data, data visualisation and download
note: Daily percentage change in visits to retail and recreation, grocery and other places versus a Jan-Feb 2020 baseline, by country. CSV, API and R/Python/Stata code are offered. Google stopped updating in October 2022.
course_use: Use as an exogenous COVID-shock regressor in a country-level retail or tourism ARIMAX (for example Austria vs Italy vs Sweden). Free.

title: IMF World Economic Outlook Oct 2015, Ch. 3: Exchange Rates and Trade Flows: Disconnected?
author_source: IMF Research Department (lead Daniel Leigh), World Economic Outlook chapter, 2015
note: Over 50 economies across about three decades: a 10% real effective depreciation raises net exports by about 1.5% of GDP on average, mostly within a year. Global value chains weaken the effect only for intermediates. This is a third-party copy; the original is on imf.org.
course_use: Example of distributed-lag time series regression; students estimate the lagged effect of EUR/USD on Austrian exports to the US (Statistik Austria, ECB data). Free.

title: The Role of National Culture in Advertising's Sensitivity to Business Cycles: An Investigation Across Continents
author_source: Barbara Deleersnyder, Marnik Dekimpe, Jan-Benedict Steenkamp, Peter Leeflang; Journal of Marketing Research 46(5), 2009; ERIM working paper ERS-2007-095-MKT
note: Ad spending in 37 countries across four media over up to 25 years. It is more volatile than GDP (co-movement elasticity about 1.4) and more cyclical where uncertainty avoidance is high and long-term orientation low. It uses time series filtering of ad spending.
course_use: International marketing discussion: replicate a simple version with ad-spend and GDP series for a few countries (filter, then regress cyclical components). Working paper free; JMR via WU-Lizenz.

title: statsmodels (tsa: ARIMA, SARIMAX, VAR, VECM, UnobservedComponents)
author_source: statsmodels developers, PyPI/GitHub, v0.15.0, BSD-3-Clause, 2026, package
note: Core Python library for the course: SARIMAX (ARIMAX with exogenous regressors such as advertising or price), adfuller/kpss unit-root tests, VAR with irf() and fevd(), VECM with Johansen select_coint_rank, UnobservedComponents (structural time series), ETSModel, grangercausalitytests, STL/MSTL. Many example notebooks in the docs.
course_use: Main Python lab tool (pip install statsmodels, no friction in Colab/Anaconda). Free.

title: pmdarima (auto_arima)
author_source: alkaline-ml, PyPI, v2.1.1, MIT, 2025, package
note: Python port of R auto.arima: stepwise order selection, seasonal differencing tests (OCSB/CH), pipelines with Fourier and Box-Cox transformers. Wraps statsmodels SARIMAX.
course_use: Quick demo of automatic order selection vs. manual Box-Jenkins identification. Check wheel availability for the newest Python/numpy before the semester. Free.

title: StatsForecast (Nixtla)
author_source: Nixtla, PyPI/GitHub, v2.1.1, Apache-2.0, 2025, package
note: Very fast AutoARIMA, AutoETS, AutoTheta, MSTL, CrostonOptimized for thousands of series (numba). Long-format data (unique_id, ds, y) suits multi-country or multi-SKU panels; integrates with M4/M5 loaders (datasetsforecast).

title: sktime
author_source: sktime community, PyPI/GitHub, v1.2.0, BSD-3-Clause, 2026, package
note: Unified scikit-learn-style interface to ARIMA/AutoARIMA, ETS, Theta, Prophet, VAR, reduction to ML; temporal cross-validation (ExpandingWindowSplitter) and forecast evaluation metrics.
course_use: Good for teaching proper rolling-origin evaluation and model comparison pipelines. Free.

title: Darts
author_source: Unit8, PyPI/GitHub, v0.48.1, Apache-2.0, 2026, package

course_use: Optional advanced lab: classical vs. ML forecasting with marketing covariates. Torch dependency makes the full install heavy; use the lighter u8darts install without torch in class. Free.

author_source: Meta (Facebook) Core Data Science, PyPI v1.5.0 / CRAN v1.1.7, MIT, 2026, package

title: linearmodels
author_source: Kevin Sheppard, PyPI, v7.1, NCSA, 2025, package

course_use: Lab on panel time-series regression across countries; IV for endogenous marketing spend. Free.

author_source: PyMC Labs, PyPI/GitHub, v0.9.0, Apache-2.0, 2026, package

author_source: IBM, proprietary, app
