title: Google Trends
author_source: Google, web tool, free, weekly/monthly (daily for short windows), normalised 0-100; R gtrendsR v1.5.2, Python pytrends (unofficial)
note: Search interest by country and region since 2004; proxy for brand/category interest across markets. Values are sampled and rescaled per query, so downloads differ between pulls; unofficial APIs are rate-limited.
course_use: Lab: nowcasting sales with search data, CausalImpact on campaign launches, cross-country brand interest. Free.

title: UN Tourism (UNWTO) Tourism Data Dashboard
author_source: UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO), dashboard, free (detailed statistics partly paid via e-library), monthly/annual
note: International tourist arrivals and receipts by region and country, post-COVID recovery tracker.
course_use: Context data and annual series for international tourism marketing; monthly country detail is limited. Free / paid.

title: M4 Competition dataset
author_source: Makridakis, Spiliotis, Assimakopoulos, GitHub, open, 2018, dataset (100,000 series)
note: 100,000 yearly to hourly series (micro, macro, industry, finance, demographic) with benchmark forecasts. Paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2019.04.014. Loaders in datasetsforecast (Python).
course_use: Benchmark exercise: students compare their ARIMA against published M4 benchmarks. Free.

title: M5 Forecasting (Walmart hierarchical sales)
author_source: University of Nicosia / Walmart, Kaggle, competition data, 2020, dataset
note: 42,840 daily hierarchical unit-sales series (3,049 products, 10 stores, 3 US states) with prices, SNAP days and event calendar, 2011-2016. Paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2021.11.013.
course_use: Project data for price/promotion regressors and hierarchical forecasting; large download. Free with Kaggle login, competition rules apply.

title: Tourism Forecasting Competition data (Tcomp)
author_source: Athanasopoulos, Hyndman, Song, Wu; Kaggle / CRAN Tcomp v1.0.1, GPL-3, 2011, dataset
note: 1,311 monthly, quarterly and annual tourism series (arrivals, nights) from many countries; paper https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2010.04.009. Easiest access: install.packages('Tcomp').
course_use: Ready-made international tourism series for SARIMA vs. ETS benchmarking. Free.

title: fpp3 / tsibbledata datasets (tourism, aus_retail, global_economy, aus_arrivals)
author_source: Hyndman et al., CRAN tsibbledata v0.4.1 / fpp3 v1.0.3, GPL-3, dataset
note: tourism: quarterly Australian domestic overnight trips by region and purpose (304 series); aus_retail: monthly retail turnover by state and industry (152 series); global_economy: annual data for about 260 countries; aus_arrivals: quarterly arrivals from Japan, NZ, UK, US. Textbook: https://otexts.com/fpp3/
course_use: Zero-friction lab data matching textbook exercises; Python users can export to CSV. Free.

title: Rossmann Store Sales
author_source: Rossmann (Germany), Kaggle competition data, 2015, dataset
note: Daily sales for 1,115 German Rossmann stores 2013-2015 with promotion, school/state holiday and competitor-distance variables.
course_use: German retail case for ARIMAX with promotion dummies and holiday effects. Free with Kaggle login; competition rules apply.

title: Walmart Recruiting Store Sales Forecasting
author_source: Walmart, Kaggle competition data, 2014, dataset
note: Weekly sales for 45 stores by department 2010-2012 with markdowns (promotions), CPI, fuel price, unemployment and holiday weeks.
course_use: Small, tidy dataset for regression with ARIMA errors and markdown effects. Free with Kaggle login.

title: Corporación Favorita Grocery Sales Forecasting
author_source: Corporación Favorita (Ecuador), Kaggle competition data, 2017, dataset
note: Daily unit sales for about 4,000 items in 54 stores 2013-2017 with promotions, oil price and holidays; very large (over 100 million rows). Smaller sibling: Kaggle 'Store Sales - Time Series Forecasting'.
course_use: Emerging-market retail case; aggregate to store/family level for class use. Free with Kaggle login.

title: Online Retail II (UCI)
author_source: Daqing Chen, UCI Machine Learning Repository, CC BY 4.0, 2019, dataset
note: About 1.07 million transactions of a UK online gift retailer 2009-2011 with customer country (about 40 countries).
course_use: Aggregate to daily/weekly sales by country for an international e-commerce SARIMA lab. Free.

title: Dominick's Finer Foods dataset
author_source: James M. Kilts Center, University of Chicago Booth, free for academic research, 1989-1997, dataset
note: Weekly store-level scanner data for about 100 Chicago stores and over 25 categories with prices, deals and store traffic. Classic data for price-promotion time-series studies.
course_use: Free classic marketing data for VAR/persistence modelling of promotions. Free download after accepting terms.

title: NielsenIQ Retail Scanner and Consumer Panel (Kilts Center)
author_source: Kilts Center, Chicago Booth, institutional subscription, 2006-present, dataset
note: Weekly UPC-by-store data for tens of thousands of US stores and a large household panel; Nielsen Ad Intel advertising data also available.
course_use: Thesis/research option only; requires institutional subscription. WU-Lizenz prüfen (probably not licensed).

title: IRI Marketing Data Set (now Circana)
author_source: Bronnenberg, Kruger, Mela (2008), Marketing Science database paper; IRI now Circana, dataset
note: Weekly store and household panel data for 30 categories in 47 US markets from 2001, distributed to academics under licence.
course_use: Research-grade scanner data for persistence/VAR projects; access by application and fee. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Statista
author_source: Statista GmbH, portal, commercial
note: Market data, consumer surveys, advertising spend and e-commerce statistics by country; many series are annual and from secondary sources.
course_use: Quick context figures; check original sources before modelling. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: WU Bibliothek Datenbanken (e.g. Euromonitor Passport, LSEG, Statista)
author_source: WU Vienna University Library, database portal
note: Entry point to WU-licensed databases with market and macro time series (e.g. country-by-category sales, financial and macro data where licensed).
course_use: Check which licensed databases contain category sales by country for student projects. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: ARIMA / SARIMA and automatic order selection
author_source: Hyndman and Khandakar (2008), Journal of Statistical Software 27(3), method
note: Box-Jenkins identification, estimation and diagnostics; auto.arima algorithm. Pair with Box, Jenkins, Reinsel, Ljung (2015), Time Series Analysis, 5th ed., Wiley.
course_use: Lecture plus lab: manual ACF/PACF identification vs. auto.arima/pmdarima on a retail series. Open access.

title: Unit-root tests (ADF) and stationarity tests (KPSS)
author_source: Dickey and Fuller (1979), JASA 74(366); Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt, Shin (1992), Journal of Econometrics 54, method
note: ADF tests the unit-root null, KPSS the stationarity null; use both to decide on differencing and on evolving vs. stationary sales (KPSS: https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076(92)90104-Y).
course_use: Lab on whether brand sales are evolving or stationary across countries. Paywalled; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Intervention analysis
author_source: Box and Tiao (1975), JASA 70(349), method
note: Pulse, step and ramp interventions in ARIMA models; basis for evaluating campaigns, regulation or COVID shocks.
course_use: Lab: Austrian tourism nights with COVID step/pulse dummies. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Bayesian structural time series / CausalImpact
author_source: Brodersen, Gallusser, Koehler, Remy, Scott (2015), Annals of Applied Statistics 9(1), method
note: Counterfactual prediction from control series to estimate the causal effect of a marketing intervention; implemented in CausalImpact (R) and tfcausalimpact (Python).
course_use: Lab on campaign evaluation with Google Trends controls. Free preprint on arXiv.

title: VAR models and impulse response functions
author_source: Sims (1980), Econometrica 48(1); Pesaran and Shin (1998), generalized IRF, Economics Letters 58, method
note: VAR treats marketing mix and sales as jointly endogenous; generalized IRFs (https://doi.org/10.1016/S0165-1765(97)00214-0) avoid the ordering dependence and are standard in marketing persistence studies.
course_use: Lab with vars/statsmodels: IRF of sales to an advertising shock. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Cointegration and VECM
author_source: Engle and Granger (1987), Econometrica 55(2); Johansen (1988), Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 12, method
note: Long-run equilibrium between evolving series (e.g. exports and exchange rates, sales and distribution); Johansen trace test: https://doi.org/10.1016/0165-1889(88)90041-3.
course_use: Lab with urca::ca.jo or statsmodels VECM. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Granger causality
author_source: Granger (1969), Econometrica 37(3), method
note: Predictive causality tests in VARs; use the Toda-Yamamoto version with non-stationary data.
course_use: Discussion of what Granger causality does and does not show for advertising-sales relationships. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Persistence modelling in marketing
author_source: Dekimpe and Hanssens (1995), Marketing Science 14(1); Dekimpe and Hanssens (2000), IJRM 17(2-3), method
note: Unit roots plus VAR/VECM IRFs to separate short-run from permanent marketing effects; the 2000 review (https://doi.org/10.1016/S0167-8116(00)00014-8) is the best teaching overview.
course_use: Core marketing reading for the VAR session. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Distributed lags / Koyck advertising carryover
author_source: Clarke (1976), Journal of Marketing Research 13(4), method
note: Meta-analysis of advertising duration from Koyck geometric-lag models; data-interval bias in carryover estimates. Koyck (1954) is the original model.
course_use: Lab: estimate a Koyck/adstock model with dynlm or statsmodels and derive the long-run effect. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: ETS / exponential smoothing in state-space form
author_source: Hyndman, Koehler, Snyder, Grose (2002), International Journal of Forecasting 18(3), method
note: Innovations state-space framework behind ETS(), AutoETS and Excel FORECAST.ETS; links to Kalman filtering and structural time series.
course_use: Benchmark model against ARIMA in forecasting labs. WU-Lizenz prüfen; fpp3 chapter 8 is free.

title: Structural break tests
author_source: Bai and Perron (2003), Journal of Applied Econometrics 18(1), method
note: Multiple unknown breakpoints in regression; implemented in strucchange::breakpoints; Zivot-Andrews unit-root test with a break in arch/urca.
course_use: Lab: detect breaks in brand sales after a market entry or crisis. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Forecast evaluation with competition benchmarks
author_source: Makridakis, Spiliotis, Assimakopoulos (2020), International Journal of Forecasting 36(1) (M4), method
note: Shows simple statistical methods and combinations remain hard to beat; defines sMAPE/MASE/OWA metrics used in labs.
course_use: Reading for the forecast-evaluation session. Open access.

title: Marnik Dekimpe
author_source: Tilburg University, Research Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Co-founder of persistence modeling in marketing (unit-root tests, VAR/VECM, impulse responses for long-run marketing effects; Dekimpe and Hanssens 1995/1999). Work on international retailing, emerging markets and business cycles.
course_use: Ideal remote guest lecture (EN) on whether marketing effects persist, linking ARIMA/unit roots to managerial questions; strong fit for the international angle.

title: Dominique Hanssens
author_source: UCLA Anderson, Distinguished Research Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Co-author of Market Response Models (Hanssens, Parsons and Schultz), the classic text on time-series marketing models; Long Term Impact of Marketing; Empirical Generalizations about Marketing Impact; Handbook of Marketing Analytics (2nd ed. 2026); former MSI executive director.
course_use: Recorded interview or remote Q&A (EN) on long-term marketing ROI and market response modeling; books as reading backbone.

title: Koen Pauwels
author_source: Northeastern University D'Amore-McKim, Distinguished Professor of Marketing (2026 CV: Associate Dean of Research, IJRM Editor-in-Chief 2024-2027); academic/consultant; Global
note: VAR/persistence modeling of marketing actions, KPI and dashboard research, co-editor of Advanced Methods for Modeling Markets (Springer); consults on combining attribution with MMM. Previously built Ozyegin University Istanbul (cross-country cases).
course_use: Strong guest-speaker fit (EN, remote; frequent speaker at MMA and MSI webinars) on VAR models for brand KPIs and MMM in practice.

title: Jan-Benedict Steenkamp
author_source: UNC Kenan-Flagler, Knox Massey Distinguished Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Global marketing and branding scholar (Global Brand Strategy, 2017); co-author of time-series studies on competitive reactions and private labels across countries; executive chairman of AiMark (international panel data).
course_use: Remote lecture (EN) on international brand dynamics; supports the international framing of time-series cases.

title: Harald van Heerde
author_source: UNSW Sydney Business School, SHARP Research Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Econometric marketing-mix models incl. dynamic models, time-varying parameters and time series; price wars, product-harm crises, economic cycles; Marketing Science Hub at AiMark.
course_use: Remote guest lecture (EN) on dynamic sales-response models; time-zone constraint (Sydney).

title: Barbara Deleersnyder
author_source: Tilburg University, Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Time-series work on business cycles and marketing (advertising cyclicality across countries, private labels over the cycle), multi-country studies with Dekimpe and Steenkamp; co-supervises PhD on business cycles and price sensitivity.
course_use: Remote session (EN) on international business-cycle effects on marketing spending; multi-country time-series case material.

title: Shuba Srinivasan
author_source: Boston University Questrom, Barron Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Applies time-series econometrics (VAR, persistence) to marketing and firm value; co-author of Marketing and Firm Value (with Hanssens, 2022).
course_use: Remote lecture (EN) on the marketing-finance interface with time-series models.

title: Gerard Tellis
author_source: USC Marshall, Neely Chaired Professor of American Enterprise; academic; Global
note: Advertising effectiveness and new-product growth across countries (global innovation, international takeoff), time-series models of advertising carryover; Distinguished Professor at Erasmus Rotterdam.
course_use: Remote talk (EN) on international diffusion and advertising dynamics.

title: Peter Leeflang
author_source: University of Groningen, Professor Emeritus of Marketing; academic; Global
note: Co-author/editor of Building Models for Marketing Decisions, Modeling Markets and Advanced Methods for Modeling Markets (Springer, with Wieringa, Bijmolt, Pauwels), standard references for time-series marketing models.
course_use: Reading reference; recorded interview possible (EN); emeritus, availability uncertain.

title: Jaap Wieringa
author_source: University of Groningen, Full Professor of Research Methods in Business, chair of Marketing department; academic; Global
note: Time series analysis, state space modelling, Kalman filtering and diffusion modelling for marketing; co-editor of Advanced Methods for Modeling Markets; multiple best-teacher awards.
course_use: Teaching-oriented remote guest (EN) for the methods part (ARIMA vs. state space).

title: Rob J Hyndman
author_source: Monash University, Vice-Chancellor's Distinguished Professor of Statistics; academic; Global
note: Author of the free textbook Forecasting: Principles and Practice (fpp3 in R, Python edition fpppy); forecast/fable R packages incl. auto.arima; blog Hyndsight.
course_use: Core reading (fpp3 chapters on ARIMA and dynamic regression); recorded talks online; live guest unlikely (time zone).

title: George Athanasopoulos
author_source: Monash University, Professor and Head of Department of Econometrics and Business Statistics; academic; Global
note: Co-author of Forecasting: Principles and Practice; hierarchical forecasting and tourism demand forecasting (international arrivals); IIF President 2020-2024.
course_use: Tourism-demand cases fit international marketing; Forecasting Impact podcast episode usable as listening assignment.

title: Spyros Makridakis
author_source: University of Nicosia, Director of the Institute for the Future / Makridakis Open Forecasting Center; academic; Global
note: Organizer of the M-competitions (M4; M5 with Walmart retail sales; M6); founding editor of Journal of Forecasting and International Journal of Forecasting.
course_use: Use M4/M5 findings as discussion case on ARIMA vs. ML; recorded keynotes available.

title: Fotios Petropoulos
author_source: University of Bath School of Management, Professor of Management Science; academic; Global
note: Lead editor of Forecasting: theory and practice (International Journal of Forecasting 2022, open encyclopedic review); judgmental forecasting and model selection.
course_use: Remote guest (EN) on forecasting practice and model selection; active in the IIF community.

title: Nikolaos Kourentzes
author_source: University of Skövde, Skövde AI Lab, Professor of Predictive Analytics; academic; Global
note: Business and promotional demand forecasting, temporal hierarchies; author of R packages (e.g. tsutils, thief, nnfor) and a widely read forecasting blog.
course_use: Remote guest (EN) on retail and promotional demand forecasting; blog posts as readings.

title: Sven F. Crone
author_source: Lancaster University (Centre for Marketing Analytics and Forecasting) and founder of iqast; academic/practitioner; Global (German native)
note: Neural network vs. statistical forecasting for business demand; industry projects with AB InBev, Beiersdorf and Hapag-Lloyd; executive education in demand planning.
course_use: German-speaking guest (DE/EN, remote) bridging ARIMA benchmarks and ML in FMCG demand planning.

title: Stephan Kolassa
author_source: SAP Switzerland, Data Science Expert; IIF Fellow; practitioner; DACH
note: Designs retail forecasting and replenishment algorithms at SAP; co-author of Demand Forecasting for Managers (with Siemsen); long-time Foresight author and editor.
course_use: Excellent DACH practitioner guest (DE/EN, remote or on site) on retail forecasting at scale and accuracy metrics.

title: Robert M. Kunst
author_source: Institute for Advanced Studies (IHS) Vienna, Fellow; Univ.-Prof. at Universität Wien until retirement 2022; academic; Wien
note: Time series econometrics: seasonality, seasonal unit roots, cointegration, forecasting and model selection; co-organizer of the Vienna Workshop on Economic Forecasting; coordinating editor of Empirical Economics.
course_use: On-site guest in Wien (DE/EN) on seasonal ARIMA and unit roots; lecture-style format.

title: Michael Hauser
author_source: WU Wien, Institute for Statistics and Mathematics, ao. Univ.-Prof. (retired); academic; Wien
note: Time series analysis and forecasting incl. sales forecasting (Umsatzprognose) and staff planning, ARFIMA models, diffusion models, price indices.
course_use: Possible WU-internal guest (DE) on applied sales forecasting; retired, availability to check.

title: Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter
author_source: WU Wien, Professor of Applied Statistics and Econometrics; academic; Wien
note: Bayesian time series: state space, Markov switching and finite mixture models (Springer monograph); member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, former ISBA president.
course_use: WU-internal guest (DE/EN) for an advanced extension: regime switching and state space as alternatives to ARIMA.

title: Achim Zeileis
author_source: Universität Innsbruck, Department of Statistics, Professor; academic; Österreich
note: Co-author of Applied Econometrics with R (AER); R packages zoo, strucchange (structural breaks) and sandwich (HAC standard errors for time-series regression).
course_use: Remote or on-site guest (DE/EN) on structural breaks and robust inference in time-series regression; R-centric.

title: Thomas Reutterer
author_source: WU Wien, Head of Institute for Marketing and Customer Analytics; academic; Wien
note: Modeling and forecasting customer behavior (customer base analysis, CLV, RNN/LSTM vs. RFM; IJRM 2022 best-article finalist). Topic fit: customer-level forecasting rather than ARIMA.
course_use: WU colleague, easy on-site guest (DE/EN) contrasting aggregate time series with customer-level forecasting.

title: Nils Wlömert
author_source: WU Wien, Institute for Retailing and Data Science, Professor of Marketing; academic; Wien
note: Quantitative marketing with longitudinal data: Spotify market entry and music revenues across countries (IJRM 2016), playlist effects (JM 2025, with van Heerde), social media boycotts (JMR 2026).
course_use: WU colleague (DE/EN) for a session on international streaming data and dynamic effects.

title: Christof Bitschnau and Resul Akay (Quantics)
author_source: Quantics, Vienna AI demand-forecasting start-up (CEO / Chief Data Scientist); practitioner; Wien
note: Founded 2020 in Vienna; hierarchical demand forecasting for retail, food and manufacturing incl. effects of discounts, loyalty cards and weather; aws seed funding; presented hierarchical forecasting at Lancaster CMAF.
course_use: Local practitioner guest (DE/EN, on site in Wien) showing how promotions and drivers enter forecasting models in industry.

title: International Institute of Forecasters (IIF)
author_source: Non-profit professional society founded 1982; Global
note: Publishes International Journal of Forecasting and Foresight; runs the ISF, webinars and awards incl. student awards.
course_use: Students can join as members via the Join the IIF page; follow webinars and blog.

title: International Symposium on Forecasting (ISF) 2027
author_source: IIF annual conference, 20-23 June 2027, Paphos, Cyprus; Global
note: Leading forecasting conference with academic and practitioner tracks (retail, marketing, ML vs. statistical models) and tool workshops.
course_use: Thesis students can submit or attend; recorded keynotes for class.

title: Foresight: The International Journal of Applied Forecasting
author_source: IIF practitioner journal; Global
note: Short practitioner articles on demand forecasting, forecast accuracy and S&OP.
course_use: Assign selected articles as practitioner readings; access via IIF membership or library.

title: ISMS Marketing Science Conference 2027
author_source: INFORMS Society for Marketing Science, 24-26 June 2027, Seattle (doctoral consortium 23 June); Global
note: Main venue for quantitative marketing incl. time-series marketing-mix and persistence models.
course_use: Advanced students can attend; programme useful to find current research and speakers.

title: EMAC - European Marketing Academy
author_source: European marketing academic society; annual conference (2026 Bath) plus fall conference (2026 Bremen); Europe
note: Marketing modeling and international marketing tracks; publishes IJRM.
course_use: Student and doctoral membership; proceedings as source of European time-series marketing papers.

title: Vienna Workshop on Economic Forecasting (IHS)
author_source: Institute for Advanced Studies, Vienna; 3rd edition June 2025; Wien
note: Academic workshop on time-series forecasting, ML and forecast evaluation; IHS also hosts the Vienna Workshop on High-Dimensional Time Series (May 2026).
course_use: Watch for the next edition; local networking with Austrian forecasters (IHS, WIFO).

title: Vienna Data Science Group (VDSG)
author_source: Volunteer non-profit data science community since 2015; Wien
note: 5,000+ Meetup members and 130+ public events on ML, analytics and applied AI; source of local practitioner speakers.
course_use: Students join free via Meetup or become members; can propose talks.

title: Vienna R User Group (Vienna<-R) and R-Ladies Vienna
author_source: Local R communities; Wien
note: R meetups (founded 2011, hosted at Uni Wien and TU Wien) relevant for fable/forecast/strucchange users; R-Ladies Vienna on Meetup (rladies-vienna).
course_use: Students join via Meetup; current activity level should be checked.

title: Nixtla Community Slack
author_source: Open-source time-series community around StatsForecast (AutoARIMA), NeuralForecast and TimeGPT; Global
note: Python AutoARIMA/ETS at scale; developers answer questions in Slack.
course_use: Join via the Slack invite in the Nixtla docs or StatsForecast README (invite links may expire).

title: Lancaster Centre for Marketing Analytics and Forecasting (CMAF)
author_source: Lancaster University research centre; UK/Global
note: Free practitioner workshops and webinars (e.g. retail demand forecasting, hierarchical forecasting for manufacturing).
course_use: Students register for free online events.

title: Forecasting Impact Podcast
author_source: Podcast on forecasting practice; Global
note: Episodes with Kolassa, Athanasopoulos and other forecasters.
course_use: Free listening assignments.

title: Marketing Science Institute (MSI)
author_source: Academic-industry marketing research network; Global
note: Webinars (e.g. with Pauwels) and research priorities on marketing measurement and MMM; expert directory.
course_use: Free webinars; some content member-only.

title: WU Institute for Retailing and Data Science - Praxisdialog
author_source: WU Wien event series with retail practitioners; Wien
note: Talks by retail managers (e.g. Amazon Austria, Oct 2025); pipeline for Austrian retail and forecasting guest speakers.
course_use: Open to WU students; check the semester programme.
